speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for seeing me. I see you've had persistent bleeding after your wisdom tooth extraction and a history of easy bruising; have you noticed any other bleeding, such as from your nose or gums, or heavy periods?

Also, have you ever been told you have a bleeding disorder or taken any blood thinners?

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, PT/INR, aPTT, Platelet_Function_Assay

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hematocrit: 35%, Leukocyte_Count: 8,500/mm3, Platelet_Count: 160,000/mm3, Prothrombin_Time: 15 sec, Partial_Thromboplastin_Time: 60 sec, Bleeding_Time: 6 min, Fibrin_Split_Products: Negative, Peripheral_Blood_Smear: Normal-sized platelets

speaker: Doctor
text: The tests show your platelet count is normal, but your bleeding time is significantly prolonged at 6 minutes and your aPTT is elevated at 60 seconds. Given your history of easy bruising and the specific pattern of these lab results, have you ever noticed small red dots appearing under your skin (petechiae) or bleeding that won't stop with pressure?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia A.

Based on your significantly elevated aPTT, prolonged bleeding time, and the strong family history of bleeding with joint swelling in a male relative, this pattern is highly suggestive of an X-linked bleeding disorder like Hemophilia A. Have you experienced any spontaneous bleeding into your joints or muscles?
